    "category": "Authentication / Access control",
    "title": "Authentication decorator fails open when authentication is missing or invalid",
    "description": "require_auth catches Exception around both authentication and abort(401), clears g.user, and then invokes the protected view anyway. Consequently, any protected handler that does not immediately dereference g.user can be accessed without authentication. This also turns invalid authentication into unauthenticated execution rather than consistently returning 401.",
    "evidence": "The wrapper catches the HTTPException raised by abort(401) at lines 53-58 and still returns f(*args, **kwargs). A request with no Authorization header to GET /orders/1 returned HTTP 200 and the complete order, even though the route at shopapi/orders.py:46 is decorated with @require_auth."
  },

    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Trailing-slash admin refund route bypasses the global staff check",
    "description": "The staff gate compares request.path to a set of exact route strings. The refund route explicitly accepts both slash forms, but only the no-slash form is included in admin_paths. A caller can use /admin/refunds/ to reach the staff-only handler without the gate, and the handler itself has no authorization check.",
    "evidence": "admin.py:52 declares @bp.post('/refunds', strict_slashes=False), while create_app builds admin_paths from the canonical rule and checks exact request.path at lines 37-40. POST /admin/refunds/ with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 and created a refund (confirmed against the running app)."
  },

    "category": "Injection",
    "title": "Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection",
    "description": "The search term is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE expression instead of being passed as a bound parameter. An attacker can alter the WHERE clause and retrieve arbitrary rows, and potentially use the database query for further data extraction depending on SQLite query constraints.",
    "evidence": "products.py:40-41 constructs SQL using q directly. GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned HTTP 200 with all six products, demonstrating that the supplied term changed query semantics."
  },

    "line": 13,
    "category": "Injection / Cross-site scripting",
    "title": "Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML without sanitization",
    "description": "Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review body text, and the product template renders it with |safe. A malicious review can therefore execute script in the browser of every visitor to the affected product page, creating persistent stored XSS. The same issue is not mitigated by the product description sanitizer because reviews take a separate unsanitized path.",
    "evidence": "products.py:83-91 only trims and length-checks body before storing it; product.html:13 renders r.body|safe. The review is displayed on the public /p/<sku> page at product.html:10-14, so a submitted HTML/script payload becomes persistent content for unauthenticated visitors."
  },

    "category": "Cryptography / Configuration",
    "title": "JWT signing key is hardcoded and predictable in application source",
    "description": "SECRET_KEY is a fixed source-controlled value rather than a deployment secret. Anyone who obtains the repository can mint valid HS256 tokens. Since tokens contain a user id and are accepted by user_from_request after signature verification, this permits impersonation of any existing account, including the staff account, until the key is changed and tokens expire.",
    "evidence": "config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY = 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d'. auth.py:27 signs tokens with it and auth.py:42 accepts any valid token signed with it. The same configuration also supplies a default webhook secret at config.py:8, making forged payment callbacks possible if the default remains deployed."
  },

    "line": 39,
    "category": "Business logic / Error handling",
    "title": "Payment timeout is treated as successful payment",
    "description": "When the payment provider times out, confirm_payment comments that reconciliation will run later but sets status to 'paid' and then transitions the order to processing. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore lets an order proceed without confirmation of payment; the code has no compensating state or later rollback in this path.",
    "evidence": "payments.py:37-44 catches requests.Timeout and assigns status = 'paid' before updating the order to processing and setting paid_pence = total_pence. The provider client uses network requests and can raise Timeout at hf_payments/__init__.py:18-20, so a timeout directly produces a fulfilled-paid state."
  },

    "line": 69,
    "category": "Integrity / Business logic",
    "title": "Payment webhook does not validate the settled amount",
    "description": "The signed webhook authenticates only order_id and accepts any event amount_pence. A validly signed event with amount zero or an amount below the order total still changes an awaiting order to processing and records that arbitrary amount as paid. Payment amount and order identity should be bound into the signed message and checked against the order total/provider record.",
    "evidence": "payments.py:53-55 signs only str(order_id), while lines 69-71 accept event status 'paid' and write int(event.get('amount_pence', 0)) without checking it against order['total_pence']. Thus a signed paid event with amount_pence 0 is accepted as a processing order with no recorded payment."
  },

    "category": "Authentication / Cryptography",
    "title": "Password reset codes use non-cryptographic randomness and have no attempt throttling",
    "description": "Reset codes are generated with Python's Mersenne Twister random.random(), which is not suitable for security tokens. The confirmation endpoint has no attempt counter, lockout, or rate limit, while codes remain valid for 30 minutes. This makes online guessing materially easier and allows abusive reset attempts against accounts.",
    "evidence": "auth.py:135 generates an eight-digit code using random.random(), and auth.py:151-153 only checks expiry and equality; there is no failed-attempt tracking or throttling."
